decisions.reason: Define-XML ADAE.ADURN states AENDT-ASTDT+1 without an imputation-flag restriction, and adae-probe.yaml lines 158-167 apply that formula to the published upstream dates. The reported nonmissing durations versus missing reference values follow that formula; adae.yaml lines 391-392 add the ASTDTF eligibility condition.

Define-XML ADAE.TRTEMFL classifies an event by ASTDT relative to TRTSDT alone. SAP page 16 additionally includes events starting before first dose that worsen afterward, which the Define-XML condition excludes.

SAP page 16 includes events that resolve before first dose and recur after it. Define-XML ADAE.TRTEMFL uses the original start date alone and supplies no recurrence branch, so the documented conditions differ.
The SAP page-32 table note includes events that start, worsen, or recur on or after treatment start. Define-XML ADAE.TRTEMFL uses only the event start date, omitting the other two conditions.
The SAP page-33 serious-event table repeats the start, worsen, or recur definition. Define-XML ADAE.TRTEMFL applies only ASTDT >= TRTSDT and therefore states a narrower rule.

adae-probe.yaml lines 328-349 preserve the full Define-XML ADAE.CQ01NAM substring tests and exclusions, with the alternative changing only SUBC UTANEOUS to SUBCUTANEOUS. The reported blank dermatologic flags follow the literal SOC typo, while data-guide page 5 and SAP page 16 support the dermatologic reading that reproduces the reference.

Define-XML ADAE.AOCC01FL explicitly selects CQ01NAM='', while data-guide page 5 says AOCC01FL flags treatment-emergent dermatological events. Define-XML ADAE.CQ01NAM assigns those events a nonblank dermatologic query name, so the subsets conflict.

The _OCC_AOCC01FL_RN helper feeding adae-probe.yaml lines 365-372 preserves Define-XML ADAE.AOCC01FL's blank CQ01NAM subset and ASTDT/AESEQ order. The alternative helper and lines 388-395 retain that ordering while selecting the dermatologic events described by data-guide page 5 and SAP page 16, explaining both the literal differences and the reported agreement of that reading.
Define-XML ADAE.STUDYID explicitly names ADSL.STUDYID, while adae.yaml line 107 reads AE.STUDYID directly. The matching STUDYID key explains value agreement but does not supply the named ADSL source.

Data-guide page 4 explicitly includes STUDYID among the core variables merged from ADSL, while adae.yaml line 107 reads AE.STUDYID directly. The ADSL_SBJ intermediate supplies other core columns but does not supply this column.

Define-XML ADAE.USUBJID explicitly names ADSL.USUBJID, while adae.yaml lines 116-128 derive it from AE.USUBJID. Data-guide page 5's AE record linkage explains event provenance and matching keys, but does not replace the documented ADSL source for this core variable.

Data-guide page 4 explicitly includes USUBJID among core variables merged from ADSL; adae.yaml lines 116-128 instead read AE.USUBJID. The one-to-one AE event linkage on data-guide page 5 does not override that core-variable source statement, and equality on a subject lookup key does not establish source provenance.

SAP page 16 specifies first-dose-date imputation for a completely missing AE start date. ASTDT returns missing for that case and has no fallback to TRTSDT; Define-XML ADAE.ASTDT's statement that the case is absent on this study explains the lack of observed differences, not the missing clause.

SAP page 10 prohibits imputing missing safety data, while adae.yaml lines 363-364 complete missing AE end-date components with month and day 1. The exceptions in SAP page 16, data-guide page 5 and Define-XML ADAE.ASTDT concern start dates; no retained section states an end-date exception.

Define-XML ADAE.AENDY computes the relative day from AENDT and TRTSDT, with separate pre-dose and on/after-dose formulas. The specification copies AE.AEENDY and never expresses that computation from the analysis dates.
SAP page 16 includes pre-dose events that worsen after first dose. TRTEMFL tests only ASTDT >= TRTSDT, and no other ADAE specification element evaluates post-dose worsening.
SAP page 16 includes events resolved before first dose that recur afterward. The full ADAE specification contains no recurrence condition, and TRTEMFL uses only the original analysis start date.

SAP page 16 treats an incomplete start date conservatively when its year and/or month matches treatment start. ASTDT completes the day to 1 and TRTEMFL compares complete dates, so no specification clause implements the separate matching-year/month eligibility rule.
Define-XML ADAE.AOCCFL orders eligible events by ASTDT and then AESEQ within subject. TE_RN orders only by AESEQ, with no upstream chronological ordering that supplies the missing ASTDT priority.
Define-XML ADAE.AOCCSFL specifies ASTDT followed by AESEQ. TE_SOC_RN orders only by AESEQ, so it does not express the documented chronological selection.

Define-XML ADAE.AOCCSFL names AEBODSYS as the SOC grouping source. TE_SOC_RN groups by AESOC, and neither the full variable sections nor data-guide page 5 makes those two source variables interchangeable.
Define-XML ADAE.AOCCPFL orders by ASTDT and then AESEQ within the subject/SOC/PT group. TE_PT_RN omits ASTDT from its ordering.
Define-XML ADAE.AOCCPFL groups within subject, AEBODSYS, and AEDECOD. TE_PT_RN groups within subject and AEDECOD only, omitting the documented SOC component.
Define-XML ADAE.AOCC02FL orders serious treatment-emergent events by ASTDT and AESEQ within subject. SER_RN retains the eligibility filter but orders only by AESEQ.
Define-XML ADAE.AOCC03FL requires ASTDT before AESEQ in the serious-event SOC ordering. SER_SOC_RN contains only AESEQ in its order_by list.
Define-XML ADAE.AOCC03FL names AEBODSYS for the SOC grouping. SER_SOC_RN substitutes AESOC, and no retained section documents that substitution for these occurrence flags.
Define-XML ADAE.AOCC04FL requires chronological ordering by ASTDT before AESEQ. SER_PT_RN orders by AESEQ alone.
Define-XML ADAE.AOCC04FL specifies subject, SOC (AEBODSYS), and PT (AEDECOD) grouping. SER_PT_RN omits the SOC grouping component.

Define-XML ADAE.CQ01NAM states substring tests plus a SOC-and-exclusion condition. CQ01NAM instead enumerates preferred terms and has no counterpart for the general substring or SOC predicates; SAP page 16's medical-review intent does not equate that fixed list with the stated executable rule.

Define-XML ADAE.AOCC01FL explicitly selects CQ01NAM='', while DERM_RN selects CQ01NAM='DERMATOLOGIC EVENTS'. The specification follows the data-guide page-5 intent but differs from the quoted Define-XML subset.
Define-XML ADAE.AOCC01FL specifies ASTDT then AESEQ for selecting the first eligible event. DERM_RN uses AESEQ alone.
Data-guide page 5 expressly identifies first chronological occurrence by start dates and sequence numbers. DERM_RN omits the start date, so it does not state that chronological ordering.
Define-XML ADAE.ADURN states an unrestricted inclusive date difference. Searching all retained sections found no instruction to withhold duration when ASTDTF is nonblank, as the specification does.
